title: Experimental and thermodynamic investigation of a solar‐assisted lithium bromide–water single‐effect absorption cooling system with a flat‐plate collector: Energy, exergy, and thermo‐economic analysis
content:
Abstract

This study presents an experimental, thermodynamic, exergy, and thermo-economic investigation of a solar-assisted single-effect LiBr–H2O absorption cooling system integrated with a flat-plate solar collector under the high-solar-irradiance conditions of Mosul, Iraq. Experimental measurements were performed under steady-state operation, where the generator, condenser, absorber, and evaporator outlet temperatures reached 90°C, 35°C, 32°C, and 5°C, respectively. The system achieved a maximum experimental coefficient of performance (COP) of 0.75, demonstrating stable operation under realistic climatic conditions. Parametric analysis revealed that reducing both condenser and absorber temperatures by 5°C increased the COP by approximately 10%–12%, while the cooling capacity increased almost linearly for solar irradiance levels above 600 W/m2. Component-level exergy analysis showed that the generator accounted for approximately 35% of the total exergy destruction, followed by the absorber (25%), identifying these components as the primary targets for performance enhancement. The uncertainty analysis indicated a maximum propagated COP uncertainty of ±4.1%, whereas statistical validation produced RMSE = 0.024 and MAPE = 3.2%, confirming excellent agreement between the thermodynamic model and experimental measurements. Thermo-economic analysis predicted a simple payback period of 5–8 years, while the environmental assessment estimated an annual reduction of approximately 1.6 t CO2 for a 5-kW cooling system. Overall, the results demonstrate that solar-assisted LiBr–H2O absorption cooling represents a technically reliable and environmentally sustainable cooling technology for hot-arid regions, with considerable potential for further improvement through enhanced generator heat transfer and more effective heat-rejection management.
